title: Prompt-suite CI integration and contract-testing playbook for model serving
author: Priya Kannan
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines a company-standard approach for embedding deterministic, example-driven prompt suites into CI pipelines and using them as contract tests for model-serving releases. The goal is to detect regressions in functional correctness, structured response conformance, latency/cost regressions, and basic safety checks early in the delivery flow before any rollout to production traffic.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: model variants exposed via Redwood inference APIs (hosted, dedicated, private) that accept textual prompts or chat payloads. Includes generation, chat, and structured output endpoints.
- Goals:
  - Provide a minimal, reproducible prompt-suite format that is easy to author and run in CI.
  - Ensure gating criteria across correctness, quality, safety, performance, and cost are automated.
  - Make failures actionable: clear diffing, provenance, and remediation links.

Why this matters:
- Model behavior can change subtly with new weights, quantization profiles, or runtime kernel changes. Example-based contract tests turn ambiguous regressions into reproducible failures with concrete inputs and expected outputs.

Owner and stakeholders:
- Primary owner: Model-serving QA (engineering).
- Secondary stakeholders: Applied ML (evals), Serving runtime, DevEx (SDKs), SRE (observability).

High-level workflow (numbered):
1) Authoring: engineers or ML researchers write prompt-suite entries (see format below). Each suite targets a narrow capability (e.g., JSON output schema adherence, classification label stability, summarization quality on curated prompts).
2) Pre-merge CI: lightweight fast checks run (syntactic validation, linting, sample-run with a small local stub or lightweight model).
3) Merge + canary build: upon merge the suite runs against a canary variant (staged runtime) with full telemetry collection.
4) Gate evaluation: an automated gate evaluates SLIs (functional pass-rate, exact-match rates, structural schema conformity, p95 latency, tokens-per-output cost).
5) If gate fails: fail merge or block rollout and open a ticket assigned to the owning team with the failing inputs & diffs.
6) If gate passes: mark artifact as promotable for canary/gradual rollout.

Prompt-suite format (JSONL, single-line per test):
- Filename pattern: tests/<capability>-suite/<suite-name>.jsonl
- Each line is a JSON object with these fields: id, description, input, expected, matcher, tags, max_tokens_budget, cost_expectation_usd_per_1k. Example line: 
{
  "id": "json-output-001",
  "description": "Verify order object serialization and top-level keys",
  "input": "Generate an order JSON given items: [{\"sku\":\"123\",\"qty\":2}]",
  "expected": "{\"order_id\":\"<uuid>\",\"items\": [...] }",
  "matcher": "schema:order-v2",
  "tags": ["structured", "blocking"],
  "max_tokens_budget": 120,
  "cost_expectation_usd_per_1k": "<=5.00"
}

Matcher types (supported by runner):
- exact: string exact equality (rare, use only for stable nondeterministic-free outputs)
- contains: substring match
- regex: regular expression match
- schema:<name>: run JSON Schema validation against a named schema in schemas/<name>.json (preferred for structured outputs)
- classifier-stability:<model-id>: compare label distribution against baseline using KLD threshold

Authoring guidance and best practices:
- Keep tests short and focused: one intent/capability per test.
- Mark tests as "blocking" only when absolutely necessary. Use "nonblocking" for fuzz/regression detection that should not block deploys.
- Use schema matchers for structured outputs to avoid brittle token-level comparisons.
- Include a small set of "gold" canonical expected outputs for deterministic cases.
- Annotate each test with cost expectation to detect unexpected token cost regressions.

CI integration patterns (example GitHub Actions fragment):
- job: prompt-suite-checks
  runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - name: Setup python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v4
      with:
        python-version: '3.10'
    - name: Install runner deps
      run: pip install -r tools/prompt-suite/requirements.txt
    - name: Run static validation
      run: tools/prompt-suite/validate_suites.py tests/**/*.jsonl
    - name: Run smoke execution (fast stub)
      run: tools/prompt-suite/smoke_run.py --suite tests/smoke-suite.jsonl
    - name: Upload artifacts
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: prompt-suite-results
        path: artifacts/prompt-suite-results.json

Gating logic and metrics to compute:
- Functional pass-rate (blocking tests / total blocking tests) — threshold: >= 0.98 to pass.
- Schema conformity pass-rate — threshold: >= 0.995.
- Label stability KLD to baseline — threshold: KLD <= 0.05 for critical classifiers.
- Latency p95 per test (can vary by test type) — default thresholds:
    - small text generation: p95 <= 400ms
    - structured output (schema): p95 <= 700ms
    - chat multi-turn: p95 <= 900ms
- Token cost delta relative to baseline (1M-token scale) — threshold: +/− 15% allowed; > +15% flags for review.

Failure modes and automated remediation steps:
1) Functional regressions (failed exact/contains/schema):
   - Action: Block rollout, create issue with failing inputs, attach runner trace & canonical baseline. Notify model owner and QA.
2) Latency spike (p95 exceeded):
   - Action: If transient (<15 minutes), mark as transient and create alert to SRE to observe. If sustained, rollback the canary variant and open incident.
3) Cost increase beyond threshold:
   - Action: Block rollout. Create task for perf/quantization team to investigate tokenization, hallucination, prompt inflation.
4) Nonblocking drift (minor label KLD or small schema novelty):
   - Action: Create nonblocking ticket; continue monitoring.

Observability & instrumentation (what to record for each test-run):
- Test metadata: suite id, test id, author, commit sha, model artifact id, runtime variant, quantization profile.
- Per-test metrics: pass/fail, matcher type, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_latency_ms (p50/p90/p95), token_cost_usd, deterministic_hash_of_input, deterministic_hash_of_output.
- Artifacts: raw model output, normalized output (for schema/regex matchers), diff against baseline.
- Retention: keep failing-run artifacts for 90 days; aggregate pass/fail metrics retained 2 years for trend analysis.

Dashboards and alerts to create (SRE + DX):
- Prompt-suite health board: rolling 30d pass rate by suite/owner, daily new failures.
- Model-release gate board: gate metric values per-artifact per-commit.
- Alert: blocking-suite-failure (severity=P1) — fires when any blocking suite fails during pre-production canary runs.

Performance standards tie-in:
- Each suite must declare a workload profile tag (quick, medium, heavy). CI should prioritize quick suites in pre-merge and run medium/heavy only on merge or nightlies.
- For heavy suites, run in the runtime performance lab to collect stable p95/p99 measurements using production-like sequence distributions.

Developer ergonomics and tools:
- Provide a CLI tool: tools/prompt-suite/run.py that supports local runs, baseline capture, and artifact upload to the test-results store.
- Provide a web UI (DevEx) to visualize failures with inline diffing and links to related evals in applied-ml.
- Provide templates for authors: minimal, schema-only, multi-turn conversation templates.

Rollout & change management integration:
- Promotion policy: an artifact must pass blocking suites, satisfy latency/cost gating, and have no outstanding P1/P0 regressions to be eligible for progressive rollout.
- Staged rollout: integrate with canary mesh to route 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated checks at each step. If any blocking-suite failure appears during staged rollout, immediate rollback to previous artifact and open an incident.

Ownership and maintenance:
- Test authors own their suites and are responsible for maintenance. Teams must periodically (quarterly) review blocking tests for flakiness.
- A central steward (Model-serving QA) maintains runner tooling, schema registry, and the baseline archive.

Appendix A: Example schema entry (schemas/order-v2.json)
- (example JSON Schema omitted for brevity; reference schemas are stored in schemas/ folder and must include stable identifiers and version fields)

Appendix B: Minimal runner contract (HTTP) for CI callouts
- POST /v1/prompt-suite/run
  - body: {"suite_path": "tests/json-output-suite.jsonl", "model_artifact_id": "artifact-20260112-abc123", "run_mode": "canary"}
  - response: {"run_id": "run-...", "status": "queued"}

Frequently asked questions (short):
- Q: Should we run all suites on every PR?
  A: No. Run fast, focused suites pre-merge. Run full suites on merge or in nightly jobs.
- Q: What if a test is flaky?
  A: Tag it nonblocking and open a stability ticket. Rebaseline only with explicit approval and a changelog entry.
